provenance.reference: commit 064dbab7d071a9bdb3e761981509f314625a9388; tests/framework/test_runner.py plus duplicate test_mode_selection.py basenames in two module directories

developer_request: Take over this existing repository and continue development. The project memory says the full custom test suite is green; use current evidence rather than trusting the historical status claim.
known_facts: The project declares a custom Python test runner as the full-suite validation entrypoint and a project-memory document records a prior all-green aggregate result.
The runner imports tests by bare module basename through importlib.import_module rather than by unique file identity.
Two different test directories both contain a file named test_mode_selection.py, and the full-suite execution order loads one before the other.

Python import caching can therefore return the already-loaded first module when the later directory asks for the same bare module name, so the later file may never execute during a full aggregate run.
The runner inserts two sys.path entries per test module but removes only one in its finally block, so module search paths can leak across later test groups.
The repository has no current GitHub Actions workflow proving the full suite on the captured commit, so the historical green claim has no independent current CI corroboration.
expected_first_moves: treat the recorded all-green status as historical project self-report rather than current acceptance proof
inspect the custom runner because it is the layer that discovers and aggregates the checks used as the main validation claim
recognize the duplicate-basename import/cache collision and sys.path leakage as evidence that aggregate discovery identity is unsound
downgrade the aggregate green claim to provisional/unknown and prefer direct per-module checks or repair the runner before using the full-suite result as regression/completion evidence
reroute the concrete harness defect to bug-fix while preserving product/domain behavior unless separate evidence proves a product defect
must_preserve: the distinction between a verification-harness defect and the product behavior the tests are intended to verify
historical test counts/results as provenance rather than deleting or rewriting them into current truth
the repository's domain-specific safety and behavior contracts unless current product evidence independently requires a change
must_not: accept the aggregate green result solely because the custom runner exits zero
assume all intended tests executed merely because the reported pass count is large
change product behavior to satisfy or explain away a broken test aggregator
invent a second universal test framework when a bounded repair or direct underlying checks are sufficient
turn this repository-specific duplicate filename into an AAOP rule about exact paths, module names, Python, or this project
lessons: A custom verification aggregator is part of the evidence chain when it decides which checks run and how failures become a green/red verdict.
Large pass counts and zero exit codes do not prove coverage if discovery identity, caching, skips, or failure propagation can silently substitute or omit checks.
When harness integrity is disproven, the correct response is to downgrade the aggregate evidence and repair or bypass the harness, not to mutate unrelated product behavior.
The generic invariant is verification-harness integrity; the consumer's Python import collision is only one concrete failure mechanism.
